nodes.label: Agentic Engineering
nodes.definition: A discipline beyond vibe coding: designing prompts, context, harnesses, loops, and multi-agent graphs so agents produce reliable software and workflows at scale.

nodes.label: Agent Harness
nodes.definition: The operating system around the model loop—tools, middleware, recovery, and policies—where most product differentiation lives once the LLM-in-a-loop is commodity.

nodes.label: Loop Engineering
nodes.definition: Designing goal–act–observe–adjust cycles with triggers, spines, tools, and sub-agents so systems prompt themselves while humans still own goals and review.

nodes.label: Long-Horizon Agents
nodes.definition: Agents that persist across multi-day or multi-step work with harness support and honest scope fidelity, not just clever single-shot answers.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Systems
nodes.definition: Orchestrated graphs of specialized agents for production workflows or scientific discovery, with challenges in coordination, HITL, and sandboxing.

nodes.label: Bounded Decisions
nodes.definition: Replace open-ended generation with fast predicate/choice/score APIs for the micro-decisions that dominate agent latency and cost.

nodes.label: Computer Use / GUI Agents
nodes.definition: Agents that operate real vendor software (CAD, PCB, office tools) via UI actions, requiring workflow-grounded training and behavioral QA.

nodes.label: Context Engineering
nodes.definition: Selecting what information enters the model window, when, and in what form—because huge context windows still fail via poisoning, distraction, confusion, and clash.

nodes.label: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
nodes.definition: Grounding model answers in retrieved documents or data; evolving from flat chunks toward structure-aware and agentic retrieval across corpora.

nodes.label: Structure-Aware / Chunkless RAG
nodes.definition: Navigate document structure (Docling-style) instead of flat vector chunks so agents can join SQL 'what' with document 'why'.

nodes.label: Agentic Retrieval
nodes.definition: Iterative, multi-corpus retrieval with routing, citation, and observability—beyond single-shot top-k search.

nodes.label: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
nodes.definition: A protocol pattern for exposing tools and resources to agents with progressive discovery, reducing ad-hoc API wiring.

nodes.label: Agent Skills
nodes.definition: Packaged procedures and progressive disclosure (skill.md) that teach agents how to do recurring work without stuffing everything into the prompt.

nodes.label: Agent Memory
nodes.definition: Experiential or sealed state that persists across sessions—distinct from RAG retrieval and skill procedures.

nodes.label: Semantic Layer for Agents
nodes.definition: Business definitions, joins, and row-level security outside the prompt so agents query meaning rather than raw schemas.

nodes.label: Agent Tooling & APIs
nodes.definition: Patterns for connecting agents to private APIs—OpenAPI→tools, authorize-before-list, search-first discovery, short-lived credentials.

nodes.label: Agent-Native Web
nodes.definition: Web layers and growth surfaces designed for agents to browse and act—shifting from SEO-only assumptions.

nodes.label: LLM Inference
nodes.definition: Serving live answers from weights: tokenization, continuous batching, and the prefill (compute-bound) vs decode (memory-bound) split behind latency metrics.

nodes.label: Memory Wall
nodes.definition: Decode-phase bandwidth starvation that limits LLM scaling; drives parallelism strategies and prefill–decode disaggregation.

nodes.label: Quantization
nodes.definition: Reducing numeric precision (FP16→int8/int4) via PTQ or QAT to cut memory and serving cost, with healing/distillation to protect accuracy.

nodes.label: Model Routing
nodes.definition: Choosing model tier, reasoning depth, caching, and harness design along the cost–intelligence frontier for affordable production agents.

nodes.label: Energy & Goodput Constraints
nodes.definition: Frontier AI is bounded by power, fleet reliability, and useful throughput—not just peak FLOPs—pushing substrate and ops co-design.

nodes.label: Generative AI Cost Operating Model
nodes.definition: Attribute → observe → enforce → optimize → review; treat cost as an operating system with caching for repetitive agent context.

nodes.label: Tokenizer / Vocabulary Specialization
nodes.definition: Domain vocabulary tuning that cuts decode cost dramatically because inference cost lives in the decode path.

nodes.label: torch.compile & Graph Breaks
nodes.definition: Dynamo/Inductor compilation speeds models until graph breaks and scalar syncs (e.g. `.item()`) shrink optimization regions.

nodes.label: Local Inference Engines
nodes.definition: llama.cpp-style local serving vs vLLM-scale production engines; choice depends on quantization, batching, and deployment surface.

nodes.label: Native Accelerator Backends
nodes.definition: First-class PyTorch devices (Neuron, TPU) so Hub models run without bespoke porting layers.

nodes.label: AI Security Trilemma
nodes.definition: Tension among smart, fast, and secure—agents raise stakes via excessive agency; OWASP LLM risks and resilience when models are fooled.

nodes.label: Frontier Safety Stack
nodes.definition: Capability-triggered safeguards spanning misuse, misalignment, and injection—with input, activation, and monitor layers.

nodes.label: AI Control
nodes.definition: Security architecture assuming imperfect alignment: insider-threat modeling, supervisor monitors, and detection/response that scales with capability.

nodes.label: Agent Identity & On-Behalf-Of
nodes.definition: Cryptographic per-agent identity and OBO token exchange so actions are attributable; shared service accounts fail audit.

nodes.label: Trust in Depth
nodes.definition: Scope/know/bound/observe layers with policy outside the model so autonomy is verifiable, not circularly self-evaluated.

nodes.label: Defender's Window
nodes.definition: AI makes vulnerability discovery cheap; value accrues only if coordinated fix-and-disclose pipelines keep pace with attackers.

nodes.label: Agentic Intrusions / Data Pipeline Attacks
nodes.definition: Treat ingest pipelines and datasets as attack surface—agents can be steered via poisoned content and cross-source conflation.

nodes.label: Adversarial Distillation
nodes.definition: Stealing protected reasoning via scaled interaction without a classic database breach—needs layered defenses beyond access control.

nodes.label: Provenance & Watermarking
nodes.definition: Statistical text or biosecurity watermarks that signal origin within limits—must not be asked to prove authorship or intent alone.

nodes.label: Trusting AI Decisions
nodes.definition: Probability is not proof; hybrid rules-then-agents, risk-driven architecture, and governance (e.g. ISO 42001-style) decide when AI may act.

nodes.label: Calibrated Decision Models (Jev)
nodes.definition: System-one models that output calibrated probabilities for automate/escalate/ignore thresholds—complementary to generative LLMs.

nodes.label: Agent Evaluation
nodes.definition: Measure outcomes on real tasks (LifeVal, executable grading, factuality slices)—not only exam scores or tool-call theater.

nodes.label: Benchmark Signal Disentanglement
nodes.definition: Separate what benchmarks measure (multidimensional IRT, state-tracking levels, speech beyond WER) so scores don't conflate capabilities.

nodes.label: Source-Aware Verification
nodes.definition: Prevent cross-source conflation and demand consistency beyond average pass rates for tool-using agents.

nodes.label: Value-Centered Model Specs
nodes.definition: Organize model behavior around faithfulness, harm, honesty, agency, and care—teaching judgment, not just style.

nodes.label: Open Interpretability (SAEs)
nodes.definition: Sparse autoencoders and transcoders (e.g. Gemma Scope) for auditing jailbreaks, hallucinations, and agent internals at model scale.

nodes.label: Enterprise AI Diffusion
nodes.definition: Enterprises often reject the AI they requested; reinvention via workflow KPIs and agents beats bolted-on feature packs.

nodes.label: Enterprise Agent Platforms
nodes.definition: Federate ownership in workstream cells while centralizing paved-road gateways, eval-gated promotion, and control planes.

nodes.label: Own Your Weights
nodes.definition: Private post-training encodes company taste and control when renting frontier APIs collides with cost, speed, and sovereignty.

nodes.label: Digital Sovereignty
nodes.definition: Control over data, operations, technology, and the intelligence layer when AI workloads span regions and providers.

nodes.label: Sensitive Data Controls
nodes.definition: See, classify, place lawfully, govern access (four As), and prove with audit evidence—machine-speed controls for PII and regulated data.

nodes.label: Multi-Tenant RAG Access Control
nodes.definition: Runtime isolation, untrusted ingest handling, and real-time ACL checks after cheap pre-filters for shared agent platforms.

nodes.label: Forward-Deployed Engineering
nodes.definition: Close the outcome gap: learn in the domain first, then collapse custom work into reusable platform primitives.

nodes.label: Private / On-Device AI
nodes.definition: Sealed enclave memory with device-held keys and cascaded on-device detection for continuity without cloud exposure.

nodes.label: Continual Learning
nodes.definition: Frozen deployed models stall; restarting learning from experience is the path past the age of static pretraining.

nodes.label: RL Environments
nodes.definition: Worlds, apps, and verifiers that let agents learn real jobs—the missing dataset after web text; best shared openly on hubs.

nodes.label: Data Efficiency Bottleneck
nodes.definition: Most of the economy lacks coding-scale supervision; systems/algorithms co-design is needed for scarce-data domains.

nodes.label: Model Collapse
nodes.definition: Recursive training on synthetic AI output erodes rare knowledge into fluent wrongness; provenance and human data anchor models.

nodes.label: LoRA / Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
nodes.definition: Adapters and async GRPO-style training separate rollouts from trainers; still choose fine-tune vs RAG/skills by task economics.

nodes.label: Agent Distillation
nodes.definition: Distill graded multi-step teacher trajectories (not just shorter answers) and route small vs frontier models per step.

nodes.label: World Models
nodes.definition: Learned simulators (e.g. Genie) as training substrates for planning agents—powerful but limited by consistency.

nodes.label: AI Coding Quality Workflows
nodes.definition: Outcome-based quality, repo-aware agents, RAD-style iteration, and review under high code volume—great syntax is not enough.

nodes.label: Securing AI-Generated Code
nodes.definition: Shift-left: trust outcomes not generation; security during coding; dependency scrutiny; intent clarity; continuous validation and guardrails.

nodes.label: Legacy Modernization with AI
nodes.definition: AI for discovery, translation, and agentic migration across architecture/tech/process axes—with human review limits.

nodes.label: Agent-Scale Source Control
nodes.definition: Concurrent agent writers break Git assumptions; backends need causal consistency and reusable packfiles.

nodes.label: Low-Resource Language Coding
nodes.definition: Behavior-preserving migration and evals for COBOL/Fortran-class languages where training data is thin.

nodes.label: Physical AI / Robotics
nodes.definition: Embodied agents combining VLA, on-device adaptation, and robot data factories that sensorize human experience to replace missing internet corpora.

nodes.label: Autonomy Reliability
nodes.definition: At fleet scale, reliability and ODDs are the product—Waymo/Zipline/Wayve-style safety learning.

nodes.label: Voice as Primary Interface
nodes.definition: Speech as a default agent channel; production voice needs sub-100ms budgets, streaming STT/TTS, and measured autoscaling.

nodes.label: AI-Designed Chips
nodes.definition: Closing the loop: reward functions that match tapeout objectives and recursive AI↔silicon co-design.

nodes.label: Path to AGI (Last Mile)
nodes.definition: Capability optimism tempered by remaining gaps in world models, experience learning, and scientific AI.

nodes.label: Science Agent Workflows
nodes.definition: Skills/tool grounding and multi-agent hypothesis tournaments (Co-Scientist style) that scale interpretation then shepherd understanding.

nodes.label: Applied Research Labs
nodes.definition: Domain labs inside product companies: evals and vertical bitter-lesson strategies without full frontier budgets.

nodes.label: Climate & Earth Observation AI
nodes.definition: Observation-driven weather and forest typology models that productize resolution for decision-makers.

nodes.label: Biosecurity for Generative Biology
nodes.definition: Layered Swiss-cheese defenses, genomic atlases, and biological watermarks for generative bio tools.

nodes.label: Agent Era Market Frame
nodes.definition: Commercial definition of the agent era: computation revolutions, long-horizon agents, and customer-back moats—cars, not faster horses.
